purpose: Record the preferred machine-readable and critical-edition baselines for the first Flood calibration before feature extraction.

baselines.preferred_critical_baseline: Nathan Wasserman, The Flood: The Akkadian Sources: A New Edition, Commentary, and a Literary Discussion, OBO 290, 2020
baselines.reason: Peer-reviewed synoptic edition collecting the Akkadian flood sources from Old Babylonian through Neo-Assyrian/Neo-Babylonian, including Gilgamesh XI, with philological commentary and glossary.
baselines.access_note: Publisher identifies the book as open access.
baselines.topa_use: Use source-by-source witnesses; do not flatten the Akkadian flood corpus into one composite witness.

baselines.preferred_critical_baseline: Andrew R. George, The Babylonian Gilgamesh Epic: Introduction, Critical Edition and Cuneiform Texts, 2003
baselines.reason: Critical edition collecting known cuneiform sources; SOAS BAPLAR reproduces Tablet XI transcription/translation from George with permission and is useful as a public line-number crosscheck.
baselines.topa_use: Cross-check Wasserman's Flood-specific synoptic treatment against George's Gilgamesh edition for Tablet XI.

baselines.preferred_machine_baseline: ETCBC BHSA release v1.8.1, commit b112c16, Text-Fabric data version 2021
baselines.reason: The v1.8.1 release explicitly retains the 2021 TF feature data and provides versioned fixed data suitable for reproducible extraction.
baselines.license_note: Repository README governs data reuse; commercial restrictions/attribution requirements must be respected independently of code licensing.
baselines.topa_use: Freeze Genesis 6:5-9:17 from data version 2021 as the received-text baseline; source-critical partitions are sensitivity models and may not rewrite the base packet.

baselines.reason: Versioned UTF-8 Arabic text with explicit distribution terms and a stable download surface.
baselines.license: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 with verbatim-copy requirement; changing the text is not allowed.
baselines.topa_use: Freeze Q 11:25-49 from the verbatim Uthmani v1.1 source. Any normalization/tokenization is a separately hashed derived layer.

baselines.preferred_machine_baseline: GRETIL Satapatha-Brahmana, Madhyamdina recension, Book 1 file sb_01_u.htm
baselines.catalogue_attribution: GRETIL catalogue entry says input by John Robert Gardner.
baselines.file_header_attribution: The actual Book 1 file says: Data input by H.S. Ananthanarayana and W. P. Lehman.
baselines.reason: The catalogue and actual file header disagree on input attribution. The exact file and locus can still be frozen, but provenance must preserve both statements until resolved.
baselines.topa_use: Freeze Madhyamdina 1.8.1.[1]-[10] as the focal Manu-flood narrative; preserve 1.8.1.[11]+ as adjacent ritual exposition, not automatically part of the flood feature packet.

anti_bias_rules: A newer edition does not erase older witness history; citations and variant readings remain traceable.
Machine-readable convenience does not outrank critical philology.
Derived normalization layers must be hash-linked to the immutable source text.
No cross-language lexical score is permitted from English/Russian/Ukrainian translations alone.
If two defensible editions materially change a feature, mark the feature EDITION_SENSITIVE rather than choosing the favorable reading.
If catalogue metadata and file-internal provenance disagree, preserve both and block silent attribution repair.
